title: introduce-shadow-sensitivity-run-ci-hook-and-semantic-diff-reporter
author: Sofia Patel
description:
Summary: Adds a non-blocking 'shadow' evaluation run to the CI pipeline that computes a per-cohort sensitivity score using a blended metric (embedding cosine divergence + token-level KL-style divergence). The hook reports a smoothed sensitivity signal to the CI reporter and can optionally fail the gated pipeline when a configurable sensitivity threshold is exceeded for any monitored prompt cohort.

Motivation: We've seen intermittent prompt-set regressions that do not trigger traditional scalar metric thresholds (accuracy/f1) because the failure signal is semantically distributed. This adds a semantic-first guard that detects when model outputs drift in meaning even if token-level exact matches remain acceptable.

What this PR changes:
- New CI hook: ci/hooks/shadow_sensitivity_runner.py — orchestrates a shadow eval run against the changed code path, collects outputs, computes per-prompt and per-cohort sensitivity scores, applies exponential smoothing, and emits a compact report.
- New reporter: eval_harness/reporters/semantic_diff_reporter.py — implements embedding-based distance + token divergence fusion and human-readable failure summarization (top-k offending prompts and explanatory diffs).
- CI pipeline integration: .github/workflows/sensitivity-ci.yml and ci/configs/sensitivity-ci.yml — the pipeline runs the shadow hook in parallel to unit/integration tests; by default the job is informative, but repositories can opt into fail-on-threshold via a repo-level config.
- Tests: tests/test_shadow_run.py, tests/test_semantic_diff.py — synthetic cohorts to validate scoring edge cases, smoothing behavior, and reporter output format.
- Docs and examples: docs/ci-shadow-run.md, examples/prompt-cohorts/sample_cohort.csv — usage, configuration knobs, and recommended thresholds for common prompt families.

Implementation notes:
- Scoring: per-prompt score = alpha * normalized_embedding_cosine + (1 - alpha) * normalized_token_divergence. Values normalized to [0,1] before fusion.
- Cohort aggregation: trimmed-mean across prompts, plus a high-percentile tail-check (95th) to ensure single outliers don't dominate the aggregate signal.
- Smoothing: exponential moving average with configurable decay; default half-life chosen to balance sensitivity and noise for our production prompt cadence.
- Resource profile: shadow runs are configured to run at low priority and with a sample rate; default sampling is 10% of test cohort to keep cost under control.
- Backfill/Followups: when a cohort sensitivity exceeds threshold, the reporter marks prompts for prioritized backfill tests and annotates the Linear ticket template that the template CI automation can create.

Checklist: [x] Add core runner logic and reporter [x] Add unit tests and coverage [x] Wire up GitHub Actions job and config template [x] Add developer docs and sample cohort [x] Validate default thresholds on internal prompt sets

Review conversation excerpts (selected, condensed into a single continuous narrative): "Rishi Gupta (reviewer): Nice approach. Two asks before merge: 1) make the sample rate configurable per-workspace and ensure it defaults to off for small forks; 2) clarify the normalization math in the comments (I had to trace several steps)." "Author (Sofia): Addressed both — added repo-level sampling override and expanded inline math with references to util functions. Updated tests to assert the sampling config is respected." "Marianne Klein (reviewer): The smoothing half-life feels aggressive for low-volume cohorts; can we expose that as a knob and document recommended ranges? Also please add a small end-to-end smoke test in CI to exercise the reporter output format." "Author (Sofia): Exposed smoothing decay via ci/configs/sensitivity-ci.yml and added the smoke test job in the GH Actions workflow. Tests added and passing locally." "Ethan Walker (reviewer): Lint and typing failures on first CI run. Reran after fixes, green." 

CI summary:
- Initial run: lint failed (flake8), unit test timeout on heavy synthetic case
- After fix commit: CI green, sensitivity smoke job passed and produced the expected compact report artifact (reports/semantic-sensitivity-2026-02-16.json).

Merge decision: Approved by Rishi and Marianne after fixes. Squash-and-merge performed by release-bot. Merge metadata: merge method = squash, merged_by = release-bot, merged_at = 2026-02-16.

Backwards compatibility and rollout: The hook is opt-in for failure. Default behavior is reporting-only. We ship a config template and recommended thresholds for teams to adopt gradually (report -> warn -> fail).

Monitoring and alerting: The reporter emits a compact JSON artifact with cohort scores and a human-readable summary. We wire the artifact to the existing CI artifact store and to the internal Linear automation which can open an ENG ticket template when a cohort exceeds a conservative threshold.

Risks and mitigations:
- False positives on paraphrastic outputs: mitigated by dual-metric fusion (embedding + token divergence) and smoothing; recommended thresholds are conservative.
- Cost: shadow runs sample by default and are low priority; we included guidance in docs for teams with tight budgets.

Local testing notes: Run `pytest tests/test_shadow_run.py::test_smoke -k quick` for a fast smoke check.

Release notes: "Add optional shadow-sensitivity CI hook and semantic-diff reporter to detect semantic regressions in prompt cohorts; reporting-only by default; configurable failure gates and sampling."

Related: ENG-1428 (prompt-regression-program), ENG-1491 (ci-observability).
